messages:
ana: quick flag from nightly perf: FlashSplit-paged selected for 8k reg test, but tokens/sec dropped ~18% when fused RoPE + ALiBi hooks are enabled.
liam: which nightly run id?
ana: 1785126789, batch=3, kv_paged=true, seq_len mode=long (peak ~7.5k). kernel selector favored FlashSplit-paged due to memory pressure.
priya: did you capture profiler + kernel traces?
ana: yes. pasted snippet below.
ana: ```
Run X (FlashSplit-paged, fused RoPE=ON, ALiBi=ON):
  throughput: 9.2k toks/s
  gpu_util: 61%
  avg_kernel_latency(attn): 2.8ms
  kv_page_lookup_stall: 3.3ms
  warp_idle_due_to_branch: high (esp heads with dim%4!=0)

Run Y (FlashSplit-nonpaged, fused RoPE=ON, ALiBi=ON):
  throughput: 11.1k toks/s
  gpu_util: 79%
  avg_kernel_latency(attn): 1.9ms
  kv_page_lookup_stall: 0.6ms

Run Z (FlashSplit-paged, fused RoPE=OFF, ALiBi=OFF):
  throughput: 10.8k toks/s
```
ana: flamegraph shows heavy time in attention kernel bookkeeping when both rotary and alibi codepaths run; many conditional checks per head.
liam: interesting. fused RoPE already scales query/key by per-position trig factors; ALiBi does a bias based on relative distance. If both are separate, we might be doing extra per-token memory ops.
priya: can we push ALiBi into the rotary multiply? conceptually we could fold bias offsets into the rotary complex multiplier but need to prove math equivalence (and numerical stability).
liam: short-term: add a kernel-selector rule to deprioritize paged FlashSplit when fused_rope && alibi && kv_paged && seq_len>2048. Longer-term: patch paged kernel to merge ops.
ana: I prototyped a selector tweak locally: decrease paged score by 0.25 for that predicate. Nightly rerun shows throughput back to ~10.9k.
priya: nice. does disable change correctness?
ana: no semantics change, it's pure routing fallback. tests pass.
liam: for the kernel patch, we need a correctness proof + unit tests. Priya, want to own the math and numerical tests?
priya: can do. I'll derive the merged op and add eps-clipping to avoid drift. Also will test on fp16 & bf16.
ana: another observation: batching heuristics interact here. When batch size small, paged kernel overhead dominates; higher batch masks it. We should instrument batch_size vs kernel_choice in telemetry.
liam: add metric: per-request kernel_choice, seq_len, kv_paged_flag, fused_rope, alibi flags, and kv_lookup_stall ms. correlate in console dashboards.
ana: created RM-1432 in perf board with repro gist: https://short.link/repro-rotary-alibi-split (runner + cfg + minimal model).
runtime-bot: RM-1432 created, assignee=liam, priority=high.
liam: I'll land selector rule behind feature flag and push to canary tonight. Priya, sync with eng-runtime about an integration test window for kernel patch next week.
priya: will do. I'll also run a small eval suite to compare logit diffs; target tolerance 1e-5 for fp32, 1e-3 for fp16.
ci-bot: Perf harness scheduled for RM-1432 branch. Nightly will pick up the selector change.
ana: thumbs up. Also adding microbench that toggles fused_rope vs separate and measures warp-branch divergence to prove hypothesis.
liam: nice. keep notes on which FlashAttention variant (FlashSplit vs FlashAlt) shows similar behavior; might be limited to paged variants that do index remapping.
priya: noted. will include FlashAlt in matrix.
ana: thanks all :thumbsup:
